stories.title: Watermark Capital Moves Forward With School-to-Resi Conversion in Crown Heights
stories.excerpt: The 42-unit residential conversion of a former Roman Catholic school at 560 Sterling Place in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, is well underway. Watermark Capital Group’s redevelopment project at the corner of Classon Avenue and Sterling Place is going ahead at a former school campus owned by its neighbor, St. Teresa of Avila Roman Catholic Church. Site plans addressed to 783 Classon Avenue, which shares a tax lot with 560 Sterling Place, were filed Thursday with New York City’s Department of Buildings. The filing details the vertical expansion of an existing building to include a 42,181-square-foot residence and a 57,449-square-foot community facility. Signatories for the recent permits tie ownership to the Catholic Church and Watermark. Watermark, through the entity 560 Sterling, previously obtained the site’s ground lease from St. Teresa of Avila, according to a memorandum of lease filed Tuesday. The document references an initial lease signed in April 2024 and later modified in June 2025. The Tuesday filing coincided with a $16.48 million construction loan for the leasehold provided to Watermark’s project by California-based lender Genesis Capital. Wolfe Landau, a founding partner at Watermark, signed for the developer on the memorandum of lease and the loan agreement. The developer’s office did not respond to requests for comment. St. Teresa of Avila’s former school campus, which spans Classon Avenue between Sterling Place and St. Johns Place was once home to Brooklyn Jesuit Prep Middle School. The school relocated to East Flatbush in 2020. The remaining campus buildings are now leased to the New York State Court Officers Academy, which lists its offices at 541 St. Johns Place. St. Teresa of Avila leaders announced in June 2025 that its own church at 563 Sterling Place would be closing its doors, citing financial strain, declining participation and a deferred, multimillion-dollar repair bill. bullets: Watermark Capital converting 42-unit former school at 560 Sterling Place, Crown Heights, Brooklyn.
$16.48M construction loan secured; ground lease from St. Teresa of Avila Church.
42,181 SF residential + 57,449 SF community facility; permits filed with NYC DOB.
stories.summary: Watermark Capital is advancing a 42-unit residential conversion of a former Roman Catholic school campus at 560 Sterling Place in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, anchored by a ground lease from St. Teresa of Avila Church. The project includes 42,181 SF of residential space and 57,449 SF of community facility. A $16.48 million construction loan has been secured for the leasehold development, with site plans filed in June 2025.
stories.impact: School-to-resi conversions in Brooklyn yield moderate-density product in supply-constrained submarkets without ground acquisition risk, but ground lease structures limit long-term value creation and refinancing optionality. Crown Heights demand fundamentals remain secondary to closer-in Carroll Gardens and Park Slope; monitor local rent growth and renter demographics to gauge stabilization absorption risk.

stories.title: Japanese Firm Orix Provides $55M Refi for 200-Unit Seattle Apartment Complex
stories.excerpt: A joint venture among Mack Real Estate Group, Silverstein Properties and Cantor Fitzgerald has secured $55 million to refinance Swell Apartments, a 200-unit multifamily complex in Downtown Seattle, Wash., Commercial Observer can first report. Japanese investment firm Orix Real Estate Capital provided the debt, while Newmark’s Jordan Roeschlaub, Chris Kramer, Sam Speciale and Lance Tillman arranged the transaction. Located at 821 South Washington Street in the Yesler Terrace neighborhood of Seattle’s Chinatown-International District, Swell Apartments opened in 2024. The building features a rooftop sky lounge, a fitness center, coworking spaces and private parking. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Orix Real Estate Capital provided $55M refi for 200-unit Swell Apartments, Downtown Seattle, opened 2024.
JV of Mack Real Estate, Silverstein Properties, Cantor Fitzgerald; located Yesler Terrace/Chinatown-International District.
Full-service amenities: rooftop lounge, fitness, coworking, parking; Japanese capital entering U.S. multifamily debt.
stories.summary: A joint venture of Mack Real Estate Group, Silverstein Properties, and Cantor Fitzgerald secured a $55 million refinancing from Japanese firm Orix Real Estate Capital for Swell Apartments, a 200-unit multifamily complex in Downtown Seattle's Yesler Terrace neighborhood that opened in 2024. The building features high-end amenities including a rooftop sky lounge, fitness center, coworking spaces, and private parking.
stories.impact: Japanese institutional capital entering stabilized multifamily debt signals confidence in Seattle's resilience post-Amazon normalization and broader tech employment stabilization. Refi at 2024-delivery asset (12–24 months stabilization) suggests strong NOI performance in DT Seattle; validates development-stage underwriting and may tighten refinance spreads, pressuring new-start yields in downtown core.

stories.title: Diptyque Signs Full-Floor Lease in North American Headquarters Move
stories.excerpt: George Comfort & Sons and building owner Wohio Holding Inc. announced a new lease agreement with Diptyque at 16 East 34th St., a newly renovated office and retail building located between Madison and Fifth Avenues in Murray Hill. Diptyque will occupy 18,017 square feet in a full-floor lease for its North American headquarters. As part of a 10-year lease, the global luxury brand, known for its perfumes, skincare and home decor, will more than double its current 8,097-square-foot footprint when it moves from 240-246 West 35th Street in the first quarter of 2027. “As a brand defined by style and luxury, Diptyque’s decision to make 16 East 34th Street its North American headquarters speaks to the tower’s high-end design and hands-on management and service,” said GC&S Peter Duncan. “The reimagined lobby and inspiring roof deck are valued enhancements that continue to draw the city’s top companies.” Ownership was represented in the lease transaction by George Comfort & Sons’ Duncan, Alexander Bermingham and James Donaldson. Diptyque was represented by Laurence Carroll of Cushman & Wakefield. The post Diptyque Signs Full-Floor Lease in North American Headquarters Move appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Diptyque luxury brand leases 18,017 SF full floor at 16 East 34th St., Murray Hill, Manhattan.
10-year lease; moves from 8,097 SF at 240-246 West 35th St. in Q1 2027; more than doubles footprint.
HQ move signals office stabilization in trophy Manhattan locations; luxury brands pulling from Fashion District.
stories.summary: Global luxury brand Diptyque has signed a 10-year full-floor lease for 18,017 SF at 16 East 34th Street in Murray Hill, Manhattan, more than doubling its current 8,097 SF footprint at 240-246 West 35th Street. The move to the newly renovated office-and-retail building between Madison and Fifth Avenues is scheduled for Q1 2027 and marks Diptyque's North American headquarters relocation.
stories.impact: Upscale brand HQ consolidation from Fashion District to Murray Hill/Midtown East reflects office market bifurcation: trophy amenity-rich buildings absorbing high-margin tenants while secondary space struggles. This signals sustained demand for Class A office in prestige addresses; however, no direct multifamily impact unless Murray Hill residential sees downstream demand from Diptyque employee recruitment or visitor spend.

stories.title: Jay Roberts of Prosper Group: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Developer Jay Roberts is making a splash in South Florida. The CEO of Miami-based Prosper Group recently closed on a $50 million site along the Miami River in the city’s Brickell district. The 1-acre site includes 66 Southwest Sixth Street and 625 Southwest First Avenue, along with about 300 feet of river frontage. Before he embarked on a career as a real estate developer, Roberts worked on Wall Street. Among the large deals he worked on was the $2.6 billion initial public offering of Paramount Group Real Estate Investment Trust. As he builds his real estate portfolio, Roberts also is curating a social media following through his podcast, “The Long Game,” and his 175,000 followers on Instagram. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: You’re pretty new to South Florida. What are you working on? Jay Roberts: We have currently a $2.8 billion pipeline – three projects in Miami and one in Tampa. We focus on waterfront, best-in-class development sites. We’re not looking to bite off more than we can chew, and we just want to execute what’s in front of us. We just closed on a site on the Miami River for $50 million to build a luxury high-rise, and then we have a second commercial building coming that we haven’t announced, but it’s a two-phase project. We’re looking for the cream-of-the-crop sites. My background is investment banking and finance. I worked on Wall Street at Bank of America Merrill Lynch. One of my superpowers is raising capital, identifying sites, structuring joint ventures and doing deals. What spurred your transition from Wall Street to real estate development? I moved to Miami and there was so much real estate development happening here. I met a developer, Dan Kodsi, in 2019. bullets: Prosper Group (Miami-based) closed $50M site acquisition in Brickell, Miami River, 1 acre + 300 feet waterfront.
CEO Jay Roberts: $2.8B pipeline, 3 Miami projects + 1 Tampa project; focus waterfront/best-in-class sites.
Former Wall Street financier ($2.6B Paramount REIT IPO); 175K Instagram followers, podcast 'The Long Game'.
stories.summary: Prosper Group CEO Jay Roberts, a Miami-based developer with prior Wall Street experience, has closed on a $50 million waterfront site in Brickell comprising 1 acre and approximately 300 feet of Miami River frontage. Roberts oversees a $2.8 billion development pipeline including three Miami projects and one in Tampa, focusing on waterfront and best-in-class development sites.
stories.impact: Waterfront land aggregation in Brickell signals continued investor appetite for premium Miami residential despite past oversupply. Roberts' pipeline concentration in Miami and Tampa indicates expected demand retention in Florida despite rate pressures; waterfront/best-in-class positioning suggests targeting high-barrier-to-entry product (likely Class A rental or condo). Monitor Brickell/Miami River supply pipeline and absorption to gauge pricing discipline.

stories.title: MMCC Arranges Financing for Orange Multifamily Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation (MMCC) arranged $12.6 million in financing for the acquisition of Bel Air and El Commodor Apartments, two contiguous 27-unit multifamily properties located at 315-343 S. Bedford Rd. in Orange. Rick Judge, senior managing director in MMCC’s Orange County office, secured the financing on behalf of a private client. The loan was provided by a national bridge lender and features a two-year term with full-term interest only payments and an 80% loan-to-value ratio. “This financing provides the borrower with a flexible bridge structure to execute its business plan for two well-located multifamily assets,” said Judge. “The properties’ proximity to major healthcare employers, the MainPlace Mall and regional transportation corridors supports their long-term investment profile.” Bel Air and El Commodor Apartments offer studio, one- and two-bedroom units within gated communities featuring courtyards. The properties are situated approximately half a mile from the multi-phase redevelopment of MainPlace Mall and within walking distance of Children’s Hospital of Orange County and Providence St. Joseph Hospital. The post MMCC Arranges Financing for Orange Multifamily Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MMCC arranged $12.6M bridge financing for acquisition of two 27-unit properties in Orange, California.

stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation arranged $12.6 million in bridge financing for the acquisition of Bel Air and El Commodor Apartments, two contiguous 27-unit multifamily properties in Orange, California. The loan features a two-year term, interest-only payments, and an 80% LTV ratio from a national bridge lender, positioned to support the borrower's value-add business plan.
stories.impact: Bridge capital availability for 54-unit Orange County acquisition at 80% LTV indicates lender confidence in Orange submarket fundamentals driven by MainPlace Mall redevelopment and healthcare employment density. Proximity to multi-phase retail/mixed-use redevelopment and major health systems signals rental demand resilience; developer business plan likely targets rent-growth play on healthcare worker in-migration and mixed-use activation.

stories.title: RFR Buys Prada-Anchored Upper East Side Retail Condo at 841 Madison Avenue for $57M
stories.excerpt: An Upper East Side retail condominium at 841 Madison Avenue has traded hands for $57 million, Commercial Observer has learned. JSRE Acquisitions, which is associated with the Safra family and Status Capital, sold the East 70th Street unit occupied by luxury fashion house Prada to Aby Rosen and Michael Fuchs‘s RFR Holding, according to the brokers. Global Advisory founder Ross Mezzo and Ezra Saffati from Majestic Acquisitions represented the buyer and the seller. “This sale is a clear signal that Madison Avenue has fully reclaimed its position as a premier luxury retail corridor in Manhattan. With Prada anchoring this retail condo, we’re seeing exactly the kind of high-caliber tenancy that’s driven rents up and quality up across Madison Avenue over the past 18 months,” Mezzo said in a statement to CO. It’s unclear when JSRE acquired the property and what the value of that transaction was, but the retail unit traded for $51 million to Ashkenazy Acquisitions in 2010, The Real Deal reported at the time. The retail condo spans 18,000 square feet across four floors, according to Mezzo. Prada opened its flagship U.S. store there way back in 1996, which at that time was the luxury retailer’s largest store in the world. Saffati and spokespeople for RFR and JSRE did not immediately respond to requests for comment. RFR Holding recently created RFR US, an investment firm that will be helmed by Rosen’s sons, Gaby Rosen and Charlie Rosen and focus on new office and high-end retail assets. But RFR Holding has appeared to have fallen into tougher times lately with the sale of 281 Park Avenue South, best known as the old stomping grounds of fake heiress Anna Delvey. The firm offloaded the property in July for $81.5 million, compared to the $135 million it was originally listed for. bullets: RFR Holding (Aby Rosen, Michael Fuchs) acquired Prada-occupied retail condo at 841 Madison Ave for $57M.

stories.summary: Retail condominium at 841 Madison Avenue on the Upper East Side traded for $57 million from JSRE Acquisitions (Safra family/Status Capital) to RFR Holding, with Prada as the anchor tenant. The property last traded for $51 million in 2010, reflecting significant appreciation and the strengthening of Madison Avenue as a premier luxury retail corridor in Manhattan.
stories.impact: Luxury retail and trophy real estate recoveries in Manhattan signal capital return to trophy addresses and high-barrier assets; indirect validation of Midtown East/UES affluent residential demand underlying high-end rental rents. No direct multifamily supply/demand impact, but transaction demonstrates confidence in NYC's high-income occupancy and spending, which supports rents in luxury residential submarkets proximate to Madison Avenue.

stories.title: Roadway Moving, Contenur Take Combined 231K SF at Innovo’s 28-90 Review Avenue
stories.excerpt: Innovo Property Group signed expansive leases for two industrial tenants in one of the company’s developments in Long Island City, Queens. In the largest of the two deals, Roadway Moving, a full-service moving and storage company, took 117,000 square feet on the first floor of Innovo’s 28-90 Review Avenue, also known as the Review Avenue Complex. Meanwhile, Spanish garbage container manufacturer Contenur leased 114,000 square feet on the second floor of the property, according to the landlord. Innovo did not immediately provide the asking rent or the lengths of the leases, but the average asking rent for industrial space in Queens was $27.50 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from Cushman & Wakefield. Pinnacle Realty’s David Junik, George Margaronis, Paul Bralower and Brendan Burke represented Innovo in the deals, while Ariel Castellanos and Daniel Tack, also from Pinnacle, negotiated on behalf of Roadway Moving. Frank Rao of New York Commercial Realty Group represented Contenur. Rao and spokespeople for Innovo and Pinnacle did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deals, first reported by Bisnow, follow two other deals signed in May at the six-story industrial development, located near where the Gowanus Canal flows into Newtown Creek. Edge Auto Rental took 78,000 square feet on the first floor and 1-800-GOT-JUNK? leased 41,000 square feet on the first and third floors. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Roadway Moving leased 117K SF first floor; Contenur (Spanish waste container mfr) leased 114K SF second floor at Innovo's 28-90 Review Avenue, Long Island City, Queens.
Combined 231K SF lease; industrial asking rent ~$27.50/SF (Q2 2026 Queens average); lease terms not disclosed.
Innovo Property Group landlord; Pinnacle Realty represented; significant logistics/industrial demand in LIC.
stories.summary: Innovo Property Group signed two large industrial leases totaling 231,000 SF at 28-90 Review Avenue in Long Island City, Queens: Roadway Moving took 117,000 SF on the first floor and Spanish manufacturer Contenur leased 114,000 SF on the second floor. Queens industrial market was averaging $27.50 per SF in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Strong industrial absorption in LIC reflects resilient last-mile logistics and European manufacturing presence post-tariff/supply-chain recalibration. Moving/storage and waste management tenancy in Long Island City suggests sustained or growing urban fulfillment demand. Indirect positive for multifamily: industrial/logistics employment clusters drive renter household formation and stabilize LIC/Astoria submarkets, supporting mid-market rental demand adjacent to trophy waterfront resi projects.

stories.title: Kite Realty Trust Trades Grocery-Anchored White Plains Retail for $50M
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets secured the $50-million sale of City Center, a 361,948-square-foot, grocery-anchored retail property located in White Plains. on behalf of seller Kite Realty Trust. JLL also arranged acquisition financing in the amount of $39.2 million from a regional bank on behalf of the buyer, PropUp Group. Located at 5 Mamaroneck Ave. in downtown White Plains, City Center is anchored by ShopRite Additional anchor and junior anchor tenants include Burlington, Nordstrom Rack, New York Sports Club and Apple Cinemas, a 15-screen movie theater. The property also includes 24 affordable apartment units. The JLL Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory team was led by Kevin O’Hearn, J.B. Bruno and Jose Cruz. “White Plains is a phenomenal submarket and only getting better with more luxury residential and mixed-use developments underway,” said O’Hearn. “This led to a tremendous response for this grocery anchored, multi-level urban asset, and we’re excited to see where the buyer takes it.” The post Kite Realty Trust Trades Grocery-Anchored White Plains Retail for $50M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kite Realty Trust sold City Center retail property, White Plains, to PropUp Group for $50M.
361,948 SF grocery-anchored; anchors: ShopRite, Burlington, Nordstrom Rack, New York Sports Club, Apple Cinemas (15-screen).
Acquisition financing $39.2M from regional bank; property includes 24 affordable apartments; downtown White Plains location.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets facilitated the $50 million sale of City Center, a 361,948 SF grocery-anchored retail property in downtown White Plains, from Kite Realty Trust to PropUp Group. The property is anchored by ShopRite with junior anchors including Burlington, Nordstrom Rack, and a 15-screen Apple Cinemas. Acquisition financing of $39.2 million was arranged by JLL from a regional bank. The property also includes 24 affordable apartment units.
stories.impact: White Plains retail-residential mixed-use demonstrates continued viability of grocery-anchored neighborhood retail as live-work nodes in suburban markets; 24-unit affordable component signals compliance/affordability constraints on redevelopment upside. Monitor White Plains rents and vacancy for signals of suburban residential demand shifts; luxury mixed-use activity cited by broker may compress affordability supply and raise renter displacement risk if existing affordable tenants turn over.
